advances: Two projected endpoints in one prescribed direction; a cone profile can occur without full-body homothety. The simplex consequence concerns only the prescribed middle facet trace.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The common-rank midpoint has upper quantile $(Q_A+Q_B)/2$. The support deficits $\delta_A=h_A-h-\tau,\ \delta_B=h_B-h+\tau$ vary over the line with sum $c=h_A+h_B-2h$. The exact cost is $a\operatorname{clip}(\delta_A/w_A,0,1)^d+b\operatorname{clip}(\delta_B/w_B,0,1)^d$, where clipping truncates to the given interval. A full endpoint costs at least $a$, which is attained by taking $\delta_A$ sufficiently large and $\delta_B$ sufficiently negative. If $c\le0$, choose both deficits $c/2$ to attain zero, matching $m=0$. If $c\ge w_A+w_B$, every tilt has a full endpoint and $m=1$.

For $c>0$, with neither endpoint full put $x=(\delta_A)_+/w_A$ and $y=(\delta_B)_+/w_B$. Then $w_Ax+w_By\ge c$. Minimizing $a x^d+b y^d$ under this constraint and $x,y\ge0$ gives $C_d(c/(w_A+w_B))^d$: for $d>1$ this is sharp Hölder, with equality at the nonnegative weighted Hölder vector normalized to make $w_Ax+w_By=c$. For $d=1$ put all the mass of that constraint on the cheaper unit cost $\min(a/w_A,b/w_B)$. This unconstrained minimum at $c=w_A+w_B$ is at least $a$, since one of $x,y$ is then at least one. This also proves $C_d\ge a$ and the stated saturated branch. For $0<c<w_A+w_B$, the midpoint probability is $m=(c/(w_A+w_B))^d$. If $C_dm<a$, each summand at an equality allocation is less than $a\le b$, so both coordinates are below one and the equality allocation gives actual admissible deficits summing to $c$. Otherwise the full-$A$/empty-$B$ allocation attains the minimum. Substituting the root-proportional width ratio into $C_d$ gives the stated special value, including $d=1$.

For the simplex specialization, let $K$ be a $d$-simplex of volume $k$, and write the endpoint barycentric coordinate as $a_i+\alpha\lambda_i$ and $b_i+\beta\lambda_i$ on the corresponding homothetic copies, $\alpha\ge\beta>0$. The upper tails of $\lambda_i$ on $K$ are powers of support deficits by homothety about vertex $i$, so the two endpoint widths are $\alpha,\beta$ and volumes $k\alpha^d,k\beta^d$. Every real tilt with the middle facet trace is of the form $\lambda_i(x)+tz\ge1/(d+1)$. With $\sigma=(\alpha+\beta)/2$ and $h_i=(\alpha+\beta+a_i+b_i)/2-1/(d+1)$, the midpoint tail is $\operatorname{clip}(h_i/\sigma,0,1)^d$ and $C_d=2k\sigma^d$. Since $2\sigma^d\ge\beta^d$, the formula reduces to $k\min\{\beta^d,2(h_i)_+^d\}$ even when the midpoint cut saturates. The middle contributes $\gamma_d k$.

In the balanced case $\alpha^d=1+\beta^d$ implies $(d+1)\alpha\ge 2+(d-1)\beta$, since $\alpha\ge\max(1,\beta)$. Midpoint containment implies $(a_i+b_i)/2\ge0$ by evaluating the minimum of $\lambda_i$ on the midpoint homothet. These give $h_i\ge d\beta/(d+1)$. The binomial theorem gives $2\gamma_d\le1$, so the exact minimum pays $2\gamma_d k\beta^d=2\gamma_d b$. If the smaller fiber has zero volume and $a=k$, the middle facet trace alone pays $\gamma_d M/2$ for $M=2a$.

statement:
Let two projected endpoint probability laws have decreasing upper quantiles $Q_A(p)=h_A-w_Ap^{1/d}$ and $Q_B(p)=h_B-w_Bp^{1/d}$ for $p\in[0,1]$, with $d\ge1$, $w_A,w_B>0$, and actual volumes $0<a\le b$. Let $m$ be the upper tail at $h$ of their common-rank midpoint projection, extended by its usual saturated values. The minimum actual endpoint mass over all common tilts $\tau$ at thresholds $h+\tau,h-\tau$ is
$$
\min\{a,C_dm\},\qquad
C_d=\frac{(w_A+w_B)^d}{[w_A^{d/(d-1)}a^{-1/(d-1)}+w_B^{d/(d-1)}b^{-1/(d-1)}]^{d-1}}\quad(d>1),
$$
and $C_1=(w_A+w_B)\min(a/w_A,b/w_B)$. If $w_A/w_B=(a/b)^{1/d}$, then $C_d=2((a^{1/d}+b^{1/d})/2)^d$.
title: Exact endpoint cap minimum for two cone projections at one tilt
